newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit says no need to worry about health.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit says no need to worry about health.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Wednesday that it sees no cause for concern about its financial health.
The bank also said that it would take serious note of the stock market's view of its share price.
An NCB spokesman quoted the bank's senior managing director Tadao Iwaki as saying the bank's financial health was steadily recovering and its profitability was also improving.
The spokesman quoted Iwaki as saying there was no need to worry about the bank's financial health.
Iwaki also said the bank was taking serious note of the stock market's view of its share price and would continue to improve its operations in order to win the understanding of shareholders.
Iwaki was also quoted as saying there were no facts behind the rumours in the securities market on Wednesday morning.
The spokesman said the false rumours included one that the NCB would hold a news conference and another that the bank would be involved in a merger.

Stock market dealers said participants began to dump the bank's shares after Japanese government bond prices soared on vague talk that NCB would hold an emergency news conference. There was also a vague rumour about a possible merger involving NCB, they said.
An NCB official denied the rumours.

Hurt by the rumours, NCB's share price fell to their lowest level for the current financial year, closing the morning session down 21 yen at 195 yen. The shares' previous 1996/97 low was 210 yen marked on January 29, 1997.
